approach.method_basis: The root follows the basic procedure in Section 2 of [Fred Glover's Tabu Search—Part I (1989)](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf). Tabu search keeps one current solution and a separate record of the best solution found. It selects the best available move allowed by temporary restrictions, including a worsening move when improvement is unavailable. Short-term memory stores attributes of recent transitions and temporarily forbids their reversal; partial attributes can apply to several different solutions. Restrictions expire as the walk advances, and older restrictions can be released when they prevent further movement. This molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation, generates chemically valid graph-edit neighbors, directly evaluates an admissible batch, and moves unconditionally to its highest-scoring accepted neighbor. Only that selected transition updates the inverse-attribute memory. The proposal is that this combination can carry the walk through useful intermediate structures while preserving the best observed score.
approach.novelty: The molecular implementation commits to signed changes in occurrence counts of canonical rooted local subgraphs as its move attributes. Counting occurrences keeps an addition or removal visible when the same motif also occurs elsewhere; describing local chemistry lets a restriction affect fresh molecular identities. A fixed stochastic mixture of atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and checked ring changes generates every neighbor from the current graph. A reproducible rule retains a small bounded subset of the selected transition's inverse attributes, with a fixed positive tenure measured only in completed walk steps. Recorded generation obstruction permits the oldest restrictions to be released as needed. These choices test whether shared local memory can change available chemistry without suppressing nearly every move. Selection uses only the actual accepted scores, with a reproducible tie rule and a separate best-observed archive. Preparation publishes reusable configuration and needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. A passive comparison records the first valid novel neighbors before tabu filtering from the same generation stream, exposing changes in batch membership and selected states without additional evaluations. Source-relative and incumbent score gains remain separate evidence from memory activation.

hypothesis: Walk from the best supplied molecular observation by directly evaluating fresh graph-edit neighbors that pass expiring inverse local-subgraph restrictions, move to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even when it worsens the current score, and install bounded inverse attributes of that selected transition while retaining a separate best-observed archive.

finding_summary.headline: Tabu memory changed almost every later batch across replicas, while only 10% of accepted neighbors beat their source
finding_summary.insights: The replication rules out memory acting only as whole-molecule duplicate rejection or as a passive record: its restrictions repeatedly removed unseen molecules and changed actual state selection. Worsening moves can be followed by recovery and later incumbent gains, but the episodes overlap and do not establish distinct successful escapes. The separate best archive matters: on sitagliptin the final current scores were only 0.16887 and 0.20350 while the preserved best scores were 0.41959 and 0.46369. Following the current walk alone would therefore conceal much of what the search had found. Broad structural vetoing still coexists with weak average local proposals: accepted neighbors scored 0.06743 below their current source on average, despite positive average winner transitions. The passive reference has no scores for omitted molecules, so changed batches and incumbent-gain provenance cannot establish an advantage over an unrestricted walk. The molecular assessment further shows that graph sanitization and numerical gains coexist with N-halogen bonds, unusual sulfur valence and strained ring arrangements in tightly related high-scoring families. Correct tabu operation does not make those products chemically plausible or demonstrate broader useful scaffold exploration. A scored comparative walk and chemically meaningful evaluation remain necessary to separate useful memory from redirection toward permissively scored chemistry.
finding_summary.results: Both new replicas reproduced the intended graph walk and structural memory. All 2,900 accepted proposals were valid novel edits of the actual current graph. Temporary inverse-motif restrictions vetoed 7,503 otherwise valid novel draws (72.12% of such tests), changed 279 of the 280 batches after initialization, and led to 176 selected next states absent from the first ten unfiltered valid novel neighbors. Every one of 89 required worsening moves occurred; 62 later recovered above their own pre-move score, 24 did not recover despite later opportunities, and three occurred at the terminal step. Memory installation, refresh and four-step expiry reconstructed correctly, and neither new replica needed a forced release. Accepted neighbors beat their generating current score 292 times out of 2,900 (10.07%), with 167 strict improvements to the best-observed score. The new macro final-best scores were 0.49531 and 0.50903, alongside 0.51081 in seed 0. The three-seed mean was 0.50505 with population standard deviation 0.00693. Task means were 0.40256 for zaleplon, 0.60530 for scaffold hopping, 0.83839 for DRD2 docking, 0.18975 for median similarity and 0.48924 for sitagliptin. Every task finished all 300 oracle evaluations, and every final best score exceeded its supplied initial best.

molecular.headline: Aromatic templates decorated with N-halogen bonds, unusual sulfur valence and strained rings; favorable scores mask poor chemical plausibility
molecular.overall_character: The supplied evidence covers seeds 1 and 2, compared with seed 0 of the same Algorithm Node. All five tasks have trajectories, each with 600 evaluated records including 580 optimizer proposals. The output consists of locally related, heavily decorated aromatic templates: indole-like carbonyl compounds, nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione rings, aryl-linked amines and large cyclic polyamines or hydrazides. Across those families, unusual sulfur valence patterns, N-halogenation, N–S/N–O bonds and strained ring connections recur in the high-scoring products. All task digests report ring_closure_rate and aromatic_atom_rate of 1.0, alongside charged_rate and stereocentre_rate of 0.0. These are text indicators. They establish that every proposed string contains a ring and aromatic atoms, but not that every ring is aromatic, every nitrogen is nonbasic, or a formally neutral molecule is chemically stable. Mean SMILES lengths range from 47.7 to 75.3, with maxima from 59 to 91. The upper groups are tightly related within each seed rather than a broad range of conventional medicinal scaffolds. The dominant elaborated products are synthetically implausible as specified, and overall drug-likeness is weak. This assessment concerns the full combinations of multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur, N-halogenated functional groups, unusual heteroatom links and constrained ring geometry; individual familiar substructures can of course be made. The main missing chemistry is a plausible, configurationally defined realization of the favorable feature arrangements. The trajectories do not establish that any particular reactive group is necessary for the objective.

per_task.generated_character: The upper structures retain moderately sized, methyl-substituted indole-like or partially saturated fused aromatic cores linked to aryl/pyridyl carbonyl or imine groups. Their substituents are chemically unusual: N-brominated hydrazides, O-acyl hydroxylamines, ring-N–S(H) or N–S–Br groups, thiols and brominated N,O-acetal-like units. Mean SMILES length is 47.7; ring and aromatic indicators are both 1.0, halogen_rate is 0.819 and no charges or stereocentres are explicitly marked. Graph inspection of the full seed-2 trajectory finds N–halogen bonds in 177 of 290 optimizer molecules, so this is a recurring chemical family, not an isolated alert.
liabilities: N-bromination of a hydrazide and O-acylation of an arylhydroxylamine introduce reactivity beyond that of a normal carboxamide.
N–S–Br, N–S(H), thiols and brominated N,O-acetal-like units create oxidation, hydrolysis or halogen-transfer questions.
Late sulfinamide-like connections combine N–F, N–O and thiol functionality without defined sulfur or carbon configuration.
missing_features: The favorable compact aromatic/linker arrangement is present, but chemically conservative counterparts to the N-brominated hydrazides, N–S groups and brominated acetals are not demonstrated as a sustained series.
Configurations and chemical forms of the substituted saturated, sulfur-containing and imine-bearing structures are unspecified.
No unseen target motif can be identified as missing; the observed score preference for some reactive substitutions does not establish their chemical necessity.

Replacing that hydrazide connection with an O-acyl hydroxylamine gives 0.3953519239480604. These are useful local contrasts: the score favors or tolerates changes that substantially alter chemical reactivity. A different thiol/aminomethoxy fused-ring ketone also scores 0.3953519239480604. The initial conventional indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-0 best at 0.4145039882261785 already used an N-brominated indole-like imine with bromomethoxy substitution, so the baseline also lacks a clearly conventional chemical realization. The lowest optimizer proposal, at 0.01944116589877781, replaces an aryl carbonyl partner with a larger nonaromatic unsaturated ring; ring-expanded and open-chain variants score 0.05477203059248125 and 0.05668571231341881. per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 upper family combines substituted fluoropyridines, thioethers and an enlarged nitrogen-rich conjugated ring carrying carbonyl and thiocarbonyl groups. A hydrogen-bearing S=N–N link joins these regions, while brominated alkyl or thione side chains add further sulfur and halogen chemistry. The central conjugated ring is nine-membered by graph perception, not a routine pyrimidinedione. Seed 2 instead retains a fused carbonyl/thione heterocycle linked to heavily decorated azaarenes and methylthiomethyl groups. Mean SMILES length is 67.2, with ring/aromatic indicators both 1.0 and halogen_rate 0.6069. These are substantial, highly elaborated structures with poorly supported synthetic plausibility.
liabilities: Multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur, S=S-containing side chains and thioketones introduce chemical-form and stability questions beyond an ordinary thioether.
N-brominated thiocarbonyl derivatives and brominated alkyl chains provide additional reactive handles.
Some lower and intermediate structures contain cumulated double bonds, distorted rings or peroxide links; retaining aromatic atoms elsewhere does not make those complete structures conventional.
missing_features: Conventional, stable connections between the favorable azaaryl and carbonyl-containing regions are insufficiently demonstrated in place of the hydrogen-bearing S=N–N and S=S-rich links.
The output lacks defined configurations at brominated side-chain carbons and sulfur-containing centres, and does not establish a plausible geometry for the enlarged conjugated ring.
A unique missing decoration cannot be inferred from a high group that assigns identical scores to chemically different side chains.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The sulfur-imino-linked fluoropyridine/aza-thione structure scores 0.6137646155929755, unchanged when a methyl is added next to the sulfur linkage. A brominated thioketone side chain scores 0.6132067176646443; replacing its central carbon by sulfur to make an S=S-containing connection retains exactly that score. In seed 2, a decorated azaaryl/fused-thione molecule and chlorinated or brominated side-chain variants all score 0.6027037832975162 in the full trajectory. Thus close numerical values or exact ties coexist with substantial chemical changes. The seed-0 best at 0.5994428608447784 also had an expanded nitrogen-rich thione ring and a highly strained carbon-triple-bond-containing aromatic fragment. Both baseline and replication retain the same chemical-form problem. The initial fused-dione ester scores 0.548381482770623; the lowest optimizer proposal, with a sulfur-containing distorted ring, scores 0.5253369553860621, while the new median is 0.578899. per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 high family joins brominated/propyl-substituted aromatic rings to an unusual four-membered sulfur-containing unsaturated ring and an amino-substituted aziridine. Vinylamino or aminoalkyl arms and phenolic groups provide nitrogen and oxygen functionality. Seed 1 instead makes aryl-linked polyamines containing hydrogen-bearing imino sulfur and aryl S–Cl groups. Full-trajectory graph inspection finds multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur in 250 of 290 seed-1 and 278 of 290 seed-2 optimizer molecules. The problematic sulfur chemistry is therefore central to the generated population.
liabilities: Amino-substituted aziridines and four-membered unsaturated sulfur rings combine ring strain with chemically unusual valence patterns.
Aryl O–S(H), S–Cl and hydrogen-bearing imino-sulfur groups are not ordinary ether, chloride or amine substitutions.
The combination of large size, extensive halogenation, multiple reactive groups and undefined configurations makes a plausible synthesis and stable product substantially less evident than the score.
missing_features: The generator shows aromatic/amine combinations, but does not demonstrate chemically conventional saturated nitrogen rings and linkers that realize the same arrangement without aminoaziridine and multiply bonded sulfur complications.
Configurations of the amino-substituted small rings, branched side chains and sulfur-containing centres are unspecified throughout the favorable families.
No additional obligatory target interaction can be inferred from the numerical scores, especially where chemically disparate triple-bond linkages receive the same value.

The principal core contains seven- and nine-membered rings; it is not an ordinary piperazine or simple cyclic urea. A peroxide linkage is tolerated near the high end, and late structures add aryl O–N functionality or strongly distorted fused rings.
The score-tied fluoro and thiol variants have materially different chemical behavior despite identical reported values.

Defined carbon and sulfur configurations are absent, although the high-scoring fused/bridged systems contain stereogenic centres.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest high groups repeatedly contain N-brominated hydrazides, N-fluorinated carbonyl heterocycles, N–S(H), S–Cl, hydrogen-bearing S=N or S=C groups, S=S connections and peroxide links. Full-trajectory graph inspection finds multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur in 250 of 290 proposals in one seed and 278 of 290 in its companion. Every task nevertheless has charged_rate 0.0, showing that formally neutral strings do not establish chemical plausibility.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably produce chemically defensible functional-group and sulfur-valence states around its favorable templates.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically defensible hydrogen, valence and oxidation-state control, and conventional functional-group alternatives around the same ring/heteroatom arrangement. Judge explicit chemical forms rather than treating neutral charge or sanitization as sufficient. This does not require excluding all sulfur, halogens or ionizable groups.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All ring-closure indicators equal 1.0, yet digest examples include aminoaziridines linked to unsaturated four-membered sulfur rings, expanded nine-membered conjugated aza-rings, seven-/nine-membered polyamine-hydrazide cores, peroxide-containing closures and small multiply sulfur-containing rings. Favorable scores occur inside these families rather than demonstrating simpler conventional counterparts.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-rich output is not consistently realized as geometrically and synthetically plausible ring architecture.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make bounded, chemically credible alternatives to ring size, ring junctions and linkers available while preserving useful aromatic and polar-group relationships. Let task-local feedback compare those alternatives; the presence of ring digits alone should not stand in for a feasible scaffold.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest records 0.6132067176646443 for both a thiocarbonyl side chain and its S=S-containing analogue, 0.8214401673399405 for ethynyl and carbon–sulfur triple-bond variants, and 0.19506328689370275 for fluoro and thiol aryl variants. A peroxide-containing ring variant remains at 0.19340483308724274. These ties or close values do not establish equivalent chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically very different substitutions often receive equal scores, while interpretable conservative alternatives remain underrepresented.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support local series defined by complete, chemically meaningful functional-group and connectivity changes, including simpler stable counterparts to favorable templates. Use task-local scores as objective evidence without interpreting a tie as evidence of comparable reactivity, stability or makeability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task reports stereocentre_rate 0.0 over 580 optimizer proposals. The digest contains brominated side-chain stereocentres, amino-substituted aziridines, fused polyamine junctions and sulfoxide or other stereogenic sulfur centres, while the cited alkenes and imines also lack geometry markers.
transferable_gaps.gap: The dominant substituted and fused structures lack configuration and geometric specification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable explicit configurations and geometric alternatives for chemically plausible structures, preserving those identities during generation. The evidence establishes omitted specification, not a preferred stereoisomer or proof that the hidden objectives are stereosensitive.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The root follows the basic procedure in Section 2 of [Fred Glover's Tabu Search—Part I (1989)](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf). Tabu search keeps one current solution and a separate record of the best solution found. It selects the best available move allowed by temporary restrictions, including a worsening move when improvement is unavailable. Short-term memory stores attributes of recent transitions and temporarily forbids their reversal; partial attributes can apply to several different solutions. Restrictions expire as the walk advances, and older restrictions can be released when they prevent further movement. This molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation, generates chemically valid graph-edit neighbors, directly evaluates an admissible batch, and moves unconditionally to its highest-scoring accepted neighbor. Only that selected transition updates the inverse-attribute memory. The proposal is that this combination can carry the walk through useful intermediate structures while preserving the best observed score.
approach.novelty: The molecular implementation commits to signed changes in occurrence counts of canonical rooted local subgraphs as its move attributes. Counting occurrences keeps an addition or removal visible when the same motif also occurs elsewhere; describing local chemistry lets a restriction affect fresh molecular identities. A fixed stochastic mixture of atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and checked ring changes generates every neighbor from the current graph. A reproducible rule retains a small bounded subset of the selected transition's inverse attributes, with a fixed positive tenure measured only in completed walk steps. Recorded generation obstruction permits the oldest restrictions to be released as needed. These choices test whether shared local memory can change available chemistry without suppressing nearly every move. Selection uses only the actual accepted scores, with a reproducible tie rule and a separate best-observed archive. Preparation publishes reusable configuration and needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. A passive comparison records the first valid novel neighbors before tabu filtering from the same generation stream, exposing changes in batch membership and selected states without additional evaluations. Source-relative and incumbent score gains remain separate evidence from memory activation.

research_intent.falsifier: The graph-neighborhood prerequisite fails if the best initial observation cannot support generation or the method cannot fill valid unique announced batches. The declared tabu mechanism is refuted if batches are generated from a different state or proposal mechanism, if the next current graph is not the best accepted neighbor, if a required worsening move is rejected in favor of retaining or restoring an older state, if installed restrictions are not inverse local attributes of the chosen accepted transition, or if memory ages by invalid attempts instead of completed walk steps. Complete logs showing that restrictions only reject whole-molecule duplicates, never veto an otherwise valid novel move, or never change emitted batch membership despite later opportunities refute the corresponding structural-memory activation claim. Missing provenance or absent opportunities make the corresponding claim inconclusive. Forced releases without recorded tabu obstruction or outside the declared oldest-entry rule refute the memory-release rule. Zero accepted source-beating molecules refute the proposed local-improvement component on that replica. Correct memory operation and state transitions without improved comparative final Top-1 performance are negative score evidence, not an implementation failure.

finding_summary.headline: Tabu memory changed almost every later batch across replicas, while only 10% of accepted neighbors beat their source
finding_summary.insights: The replication rules out memory acting only as whole-molecule duplicate rejection or as a passive record: its restrictions repeatedly removed unseen molecules and changed actual state selection. Worsening moves can be followed by recovery and later incumbent gains, but the episodes overlap and do not establish distinct successful escapes. The separate best archive matters: on sitagliptin the final current scores were only 0.16887 and 0.20350 while the preserved best scores were 0.41959 and 0.46369. Following the current walk alone would therefore conceal much of what the search had found. Broad structural vetoing still coexists with weak average local proposals: accepted neighbors scored 0.06743 below their current source on average, despite positive average winner transitions. The passive reference has no scores for omitted molecules, so changed batches and incumbent-gain provenance cannot establish an advantage over an unrestricted walk. The molecular assessment further shows that graph sanitization and numerical gains coexist with N-halogen bonds, unusual sulfur valence and strained ring arrangements in tightly related high-scoring families. Correct tabu operation does not make those products chemically plausible or demonstrate broader useful scaffold exploration. A scored comparative walk and chemically meaningful evaluation remain necessary to separate useful memory from redirection toward permissively scored chemistry.

finding_summary.headline: Tabu memory changed 140 batches and 89 next states; all five tasks improved their best observed score
finding_summary.insights:
Shared local memory affected new molecular identities and actual state selection, ruling out an explanation based solely on whole-molecule duplicate rejection or unused restrictions. Worsening moves can be followed by recovery and later incumbent gains, but the experiment does not show that they were necessary or that the excluded neighbors would have scored worse. Most accepted edits still reduced the source score, and memory rejected 73.1% of valid novel draws. One batch needed 493 generation attempts and four releases; the first two globally oldest entries released were not among the restrictions matching that obstruction window. This narrows an efficiency question to the breadth of local restrictions and the declared global-oldest release rule, while leaving comparative search quality open.

The chemistry assessment also limits what the score gains mean: upper-score outputs repeatedly contain strained rings, reactive atom states and undefined stereochemistry, while some more conventional structures reach nearly the same scores. Passing graph validity and moving through diverse connectivity therefore did not establish useful synthetic chemistry. Chemically credible local moves and a protocol-controlled comparison are now informative next probes; neither should be inferred from the successful memory audit alone.

finding_summary.headline: Tabu memory changed 140 batches and 89 next states; all five tasks improved their best observed score
finding_summary.insights:
Shared local memory affected new molecular identities and actual state selection, ruling out an explanation based solely on whole-molecule duplicate rejection or unused restrictions. Worsening moves can be followed by recovery and later incumbent gains, but the experiment does not show that they were necessary or that the excluded neighbors would have scored worse. Most accepted edits still reduced the source score, and memory rejected 73.1% of valid novel draws. One batch needed 493 generation attempts and four releases; the first two globally oldest entries released were not among the restrictions matching that obstruction window. This narrows an efficiency question to the breadth of local restrictions and the declared global-oldest release rule, while leaving comparative search quality open.

The chemistry assessment also limits what the score gains mean: upper-score outputs repeatedly contain strained rings, reactive atom states and undefined stereochemistry, while some more conventional structures reach nearly the same scores. Passing graph validity and moving through diverse connectivity therefore did not establish useful synthetic chemistry. Chemically credible local moves and a protocol-controlled comparison are now informative next probes; neither should be inferred from the successful memory audit alone.

molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich outputs explore new connectivity but repeatedly retain strained bonds, reactive atom states and undefined stereochemistry.
molecular_assessment.overall_character: All five supplied trajectories were examined, each containing 300 evaluated molecules and 290 optimizer proposals. No Parent trajectory is available. Every proposal contains ring-closure digits, aromatic atom notation and branching; all five digest ring_closure_rate and aromatic_atom_rate values are 1.0. These are presence counters, not ring counts or proof of physical aromaticity. The structures show substantial ring opening, expansion, contraction, fusion and bridging, with recurrent aromatic families within each trajectory. Diversity is therefore moderate despite extensive connectivity variation. The outputs range from medium-sized azaaryl ketimines to larger diaryl heterocycles and densely bridged polar cages. Conventional ethers, alcohols, imides and amines coexist with arynes, small cyclic cumulenes, hydrogen-bearing multicoordinate sulfur, N-halogen bonds and peroxides. The implausible overall rating describes the repeated severe liabilities in the generated and upper-score populations; it does not assert that every proposal is unsynthesizable. Several upper-score molecules use more conventional chemistry. All five stereocentre_rate and charged_rate values are 0.0, even where the structures introduce stereogenic cages, aminals or potentially ionizable nitrogen. These observations concern submitted representations, not any unseen downstream preparation. Scores below are rounded recorded values; chemical score gradients are local associations and do not establish a binding mode or the components of an objective.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer mainly makes medium-sized indole-derived fused aromatic systems bearing a short pyridylmethyl ketimine, ketone or oxime side chain. The initial trimethoxy indole carboxanilide at evaluation 9 gives way to methoxy or methyl substitution, bromomethyl ethers and frequent halogenation of pyrrolic nitrogen. The strongest examples retain an intact pyridine ring alongside the fused aromatic core; later structures also expand or partly dearomatize that core. The mean SMILES length is 48.4 and the proposal halogen_rate is 0.9793. Conventional aromatic and carbonyl fragments are synthetically recognizable, but the common N-bromo, N-O-Br and bromomethyl-ether combinations make the upper-score products chemically reactive rather than straightforward stable drug-like compounds.
liabilities: A bromomethyl ether is an electrophilic O-CH2-Br substituent; it should not be mistaken for an ordinary aryl bromide.
Pyrrolic N-Br and N-O-Br bonds introduce reactive halogen chemistry even in the best molecules.
Later ring expansions and open-chain imine-rich products often lose the compact aromatic organization associated with better scores.
missing_features: Stable upper-score analogues that preserve the compact azaaryl and short-linker arrangement while replacing the recurrent reactive N-halogen and bromomethyl handles are poorly represented.
The imine and oxime geometries are not explicitly assigned, leaving the spatial presentation of these polar groups unresolved.

The cited structures nevertheless contain bridged cages, substituted aminal-like centres, imines or oximes, and potentially ionizable nitrogen environments. possible_failure_causes: Local score improvement remains sparse: only 9.0345% of accepted neighbors beat their source, and the mean neighbor-minus-current score is negative on every task. This is negative neighborhood-quality evidence despite positive incumbent gains.

Restrictions rejected 73.1233% of valid novel draws, reaching 83.9246% on one task. A 493-attempt batch required four releases, suggesting that broad recurring motifs can obstruct generation. Two globally oldest releases did not remove entries implicated in their obstruction windows; this obeyed the declared order but may waste generation effort.

Nine worsening transitions did not recover above their pre-move scores despite later steps; four task runs ended below their independent best archive. Worsening transitions can therefore consume the remaining budget without recovering the best region.

The supplied molecular assessment identifies repeated strained or reactive chemistry and unassigned stereochemistry in upper-score outputs. RDKit sanitization, connectivity and radical checks do not eliminate these liabilities, and tied or nearly tied scores often fail to justify them.

applicability_conditions: Applies to independent scalar molecular maximization objectives with finite real feedback and a best supplied observation that supports the declared chemically valid local graph operations.

Useful search must be reachable through the supported graph edits within the available feedback steps. Best sampled neighbors can be worse than the current state; whether those moves lead to useful later structures is unproven.

Canonical local attributes must recur across different molecular identities while remaining specific enough to avoid blocking most productive chemistry. Neither excessively broad restrictions nor overly specific never-matching attributes establish the proposed mechanism.

The method uses a fixed positive step-based tenure and bounded inverse-attribute memory, with audited oldest-entry release for demonstrated generation obstruction. It does not use temperature acceptance, aspiration based on unknown scores, a learned acquisition model or archive restarts.

The passive unfiltered-batch reference uses the same observed raw generation stream without extra evaluations. It can establish changed available proposals or next-state identity, but it cannot supply a counterfactual score or prove a long-run tabu advantage.

The supplied graph-evolution and ant-colony observations n-4fa9546e559e and n-3ab6a944e3dd motivate score-linked diagnostics. They are neither Parent comparisons nor evidence that structural reversals are a present bottleneck.

A screening replica supports claims only on its supplied evidence. Reliable score advantage requires protocol-controlled comparative evaluation and further replicas; this intent chooses no seeds, extra oracle calls or benchmark changes.

approach.method_basis: The root follows the basic procedure in Section 2 of [Fred Glover's Tabu Search—Part I (1989)](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf). Tabu search keeps one current solution and a separate record of the best solution found. It selects the best available move allowed by temporary restrictions, including a worsening move when improvement is unavailable. Short-term memory stores attributes of recent transitions and temporarily forbids their reversal; partial attributes can apply to several different solutions. Restrictions expire as the walk advances, and older restrictions can be released when they prevent further movement. This molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation, generates chemically valid graph-edit neighbors, directly evaluates an admissible batch, and moves unconditionally to its highest-scoring accepted neighbor. Only that selected transition updates the inverse-attribute memory. The proposal is that this combination can carry the walk through useful intermediate structures while preserving the best observed score.
approach.novelty: The molecular implementation commits to signed changes in occurrence counts of canonical rooted local subgraphs as its move attributes. Counting occurrences keeps an addition or removal visible when the same motif also occurs elsewhere; describing local chemistry lets a restriction affect fresh molecular identities. A fixed stochastic mixture of atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and checked ring changes generates every neighbor from the current graph. A reproducible rule retains a small bounded subset of the selected transition's inverse attributes, with a fixed positive tenure measured only in completed walk steps. Recorded generation obstruction permits the oldest restrictions to be released as needed. These choices test whether shared local memory can change available chemistry without suppressing nearly every move. Selection uses only the actual accepted scores, with a reproducible tie rule and a separate best-observed archive. Preparation publishes reusable configuration and needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. A passive comparison records the first valid novel neighbors before tabu filtering from the same generation stream, exposing changes in batch membership and selected states without additional evaluations. Source-relative and incumbent score gains remain separate evidence from memory activation.

research_intent.falsifier: The graph-neighborhood prerequisite fails if the best initial observation cannot support generation or the method cannot fill valid unique announced batches. The declared tabu mechanism is refuted if batches are generated from a different state or proposal mechanism, if the next current graph is not the best accepted neighbor, if a required worsening move is rejected in favor of retaining or restoring an older state, if installed restrictions are not inverse local attributes of the chosen accepted transition, or if memory ages by invalid attempts instead of completed walk steps. Complete logs showing that restrictions only reject whole-molecule duplicates, never veto an otherwise valid novel move, or never change emitted batch membership despite later opportunities refute the corresponding structural-memory activation claim. Missing provenance or absent opportunities make the corresponding claim inconclusive. Forced releases without recorded tabu obstruction or outside the declared oldest-entry rule refute the memory-release rule. Zero accepted source-beating molecules refute the proposed local-improvement component on that replica. Correct memory operation and state transitions without improved comparative final Top-1 performance are negative score evidence, not an implementation failure.

Generate each proposal batch from that one current graph using a fixed stochastic mixture of direct atom-identity and bond-order edits, atom additions/deletions, and chemically checked ring opening/closure or related local graph operations. For a passive diagnostic, record the first announced-batch-size distinct valid globally unseen neighbors in the same actual raw generation stream before applying tabu. This is a within-current-state comparison of batch membership; it never selects proposals, receives additional oracle calls or supplies invented scores. research_intent.mechanism: Walk from the best supplied molecular observation by directly evaluating fresh graph-edit neighbors that pass expiring inverse local-subgraph restrictions, move to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even when it worsens the current score, and install bounded inverse attributes of that selected transition while retaining a separate best-observed archive.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: This root has no Parent. Observation n-4fa9546e559e confirms active graph evolution but reports that most accepted offspring did not exceed their generating parents. Observation n-3ab6a944e3dd confirms extensive reuse of reinforced local construction components while recording few later incumbent gains. These motivate separating useful graph transitions and score gains from memory activity alone. Neither observation establishes that structural reversals currently limit search or that tabu restrictions improve this benchmark. The untested claim is that best-admissible-neighbor walking with short-lived local reversal restrictions can traverse useful intermediate structures despite sparse whole-molecule feedback.
